panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a T2-weighted MRI image from a 43-year-old female with PBC and demonstrates the captioned periportal halo sign, a characteristic PBC manifestation. B: Panel B is a portal venous phase MRI image from a 53-year-old female with PBC and demonstrates the captioned periportal lesions/halo sign, which are nonenhancing.

This sign may be correlated with the deposition of fibrous tissue and parenchymal extinction around the portal triads. The portal halo sign is the most typical feature of PBC, although it may sometimes also be found in autoimmune hepatitis-PBC overlap [51]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Patient MRI in a 53-year-old woman with explicitly captioned stage IV PBC demonstrates a nodular liver surface and irregular hepatic contour, supporting cirrhotic liver morphology. [raw subtype: stage IV PBC] b: The captioned T2-weighted MRI directly demonstrates periportal hyperintensity and periportal halo signs in a patient with stage IV PBC. [raw subtype: stage IV PBC] c: The caption attributes this portal-venous-phase MRI to stage IV PBC and specifically identifies rounded low-signal lesions without obvious enhancement. These lesions are not represented in the allowed vocabulary. [raw subtype: stage IV PBC] d: MRCP from the explicitly captioned stage IV PBC patient demonstrates the disease-associated irregular configuration and segmental dilatation of medium to small bile ducts. The finding is absent from the allowed vocabulary. [raw subtype: stage IV PBC]

panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced MRI in a 53-year-old female with PBC (stage IV, Ludwig staging system) (a–d). The T1WI image shows the liver surface nodularity with an irregular contour (a). The T2WI image shows periportal hyperintensity (arrows) and periportal halo signs (*) (b). The PVP image shows the rounded low signal intensity lesions with no obvious enhancement (*) (c), and the MRCP image shows segmental irregular dilatation of the medium to small bile ducts (d)
in_text_mentions: Overall, there are several pathological changes throughout the disease process of PBC that can be captured and monitored by imaging (Figs. 6, 7, and 8). In terms of the CT /MR imaging features, some are relatively unique to PBC, such as liver parenchyma heterogeneity, periportal halo sign, irregular configuration of the small to medium biliary ducts and lymphadenopathy. These features can be better demonstrated on MRI and deserve the attention of radiologists.
